question: Should OpenClaw sponsor Discord source-message subagent progress as a bundled feature with the proposed config and generic channel lifecycle/delivery-context API additions?
rationale: The implementation is plausible and well-proven, but it creates new user-facing configuration and permanent Plugin SDK contracts whose scope and ownership cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Sponsor and narrow
options.body: Approve the feature while requiring owners to minimize the generic API and config surface before resolving conflicts and landing it.

options.title: Sponsor current contract
options.body: Accept the proposed lifecycle, delivery-context, and configuration surfaces as the intended permanent bundled Discord contract.

options.title: Decline core expansion
options.body: Close the PR and keep subagent visibility on existing progress drafts or a future plugin-local mechanism that needs no new generic core contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and narrow
recommendation.body: Approve the feature while requiring owners to minimize the generic API and config surface before resolving conflicts and landing it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans both subagent completion delivery and channel progress behavior.
